purpose: Validate official Bybit linear orderbook.200 daily archives with explicit, narrowly versioned first-snapshot and terminal-boundary partition rules, while remaining fail-closed on all other integrity failures.

first_snapshot_partition.name: first_snapshot_dual_timestamp_pre_start_partition_v1
allowed_only_when: the record is the first non-empty archive record
each of ts and cts is at or after target_day_start_ms or no earlier than target_day_start_ms - 2000
at least one timestamp is before target_day_start_ms when the exception is recorded
every later record has ts >= target_day_start_ms and cts >= target_day_start_ms
ts and cts remain non-decreasing across the full archive
no other timestamp or boundary error exists

terminal_duplicate_partition.name: terminal_delta_snapshot_duplicate_end_partition_v1
allowed_only_when: the record is the final non-empty archive record
the record's (u, seq) pair exactly equals the immediately preceding record's pair
the immediately preceding record type is delta or snapshot
the overrun is greater than the ordinary 2000 ms grace and no greater than 2001 ms
all other records have max(ts, cts) - target_day_end_ms <= 2000 ms or are covered only by this terminal exception
all sequence, timestamp ordering, topic, symbol, level-shape, JSON, ZIP, and duplicate checks pass
rejected_when: the overrun is greater than 2001 ms
the overrun occurs on any non-final record
the final record is not a snapshot
the final pair is not an exact terminal duplicate
any other boundary or integrity error exists
terminal_duplicate_partition.rationale: The official Bybit daily archive convention can include a terminal delta-plus-snapshot duplicate whose exchange timestamps straddle the exclusive UTC-day partition by a narrowly bounded amount. The 2,001 ms cap is an explicit versioned acceptance boundary, not a general timestamp relaxation.

snapshot_reset_rule.name: bybit_documented_u1_service_restart_v2
allowed_only_when: exactly one mid-stream record is type == snapshot and u == 1
the reset snapshot seq is strictly greater than the immediately previous seq
the immediately following record has u == 2
all seq values are strictly increasing except the existing terminal snapshot duplicate convention
all other u values are strictly increasing except the existing terminal snapshot duplicate convention

integrity_requirements: ZIP opens successfully and CRC/inflate checks pass
JSONL parses for every non-empty record
topic and symbol match the requested symbol
record type is snapshot or delta
ts and cts are integer milliseconds
u and seq are integer values
u and seq are strictly ordered under the documented exceptions
ordinary timestamps and boundaries are checked without broad grace expansion
source archive SHA-256 is recorded before Drive upload
Drive upload uses the symbol-specific raw folder
Drive restore is by immutable file ID
restored byte count and SHA-256 exactly match the source
operational_instruction: Do not modify the original validator or v2/v3/v4 validators in place.
Run validate_bybit_l2_archive_historical_v5.py for every unaccepted new archive after this rule is adopted by the checkpointed worker.
Record the exact boundary exception event in the validation result and manifest.
If validation, upload, restore, or hash verification fails, record the failure and stop the worker.
Do not invent a wider timestamp window, skip records, reconstruct data, or substitute another exchange.
Do not reprocess accepted archives unless an explicit provenance audit requires it.
Do not start Phase 2, Phase 3, Phase 4, trading, alerts, or deployment during Phase 1 acquisition.
